chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the funerals of men, children, and women, he (peace be upon him) said: 'The women are placed closest to the Qiblah, the children are placed below them, and the men are placed beyond that, and the Imam stands opposite the men.'
ai.seo_question: How are men, women, and children arranged during a funeral prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the canonical spatial hierarchy for Salat al-Janazah, reflecting the Shia juristic view of gender and age-based precedence in congregational prayer. The arrangement places women closest to the Qiblah, followed by children, with men positioned furthest away, while the Imam stands opposite the men, mirroring the general prayer layout but adapted for the deceased. This specific ordering underscores the theological emphasis on modesty and the distinct roles within the community during funeral rites.
